examples.knowledge_point: Computing Second Order Derivatives Using Leibnitz Notation
examples.problem: Calculate $\dfrac {\textrm d^2 y}{\textrm d x^2}$ for $y = 3 x^4 + 5x+ \sqrt x.$
examples.worked_solution:
Computing the first derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{x}^{4}+5x+\sqrt{x}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{x}^{4}+5x+{x}^{1/2}) \\  & =3(4){x}^{3}+5+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{-1/2} \\  & =12{x}^{3}+5+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{-1/2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the second derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(12{x}^{3}+5+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{-1/2}) \\  & =12(3){x}^{2}+0+\frac{1}{2}(-\frac{1}{2}){x}^{-3/2} \\  & =36{x}^{2}-\frac{1}{4}{x}^{-3/2}.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
Computing the first derivative, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={(2{x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}-7)}^{′} &  \\  & =3\cdot 2{x}^{2}+2\cdot 4x-0 \\  & =6{x}^{2}+8x\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the second derivative, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x) & ={(6{x}^{2}+8x)}^{′} \\  & =2\cdot 6x+8 \\  & =12x+8\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating the second derivative at $x=-2$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(-2) & =12(-2)+8 \\  & =-24+8 \\  & =-16.\end{aligned}
$$
